text.p: Commerzbank AG, Germany's third largest commercial bank, reported on Monday a 24 percent rise in net profits for 1996 due to strong financial operations and strict cost control.
The bank also announced plans to seek shareholder approval for future capital raising measures including a possible 200 million mark ($120 million) share issue.

In a statement before its annual results news conference on Tuesday, Commerzbank said its net profit for last year was 1.214 billion mark, confirming its intention to pay an unchanged dividend of 1.35 marks per share.
In January, Commerzbank had estimated its 1996 net profit figure at 1.19 billion marks.

Operating earnings rose 28.6 percent to 1.869 billion marks while pre-tax earnings rose 50.5 percent to 1.795 billion. "The basis for the strong earnings growth was dynamic financial operations accompanied by rigid cost discipline," Commerzbank said.
"On the other hand, the continued upward trend for corporate insolvencies led to a notable increase in provision for lending risks."
Commerzbank said it set aside 1.216 billion marks for leanding risks after deducting earnings from securities held for liquidity purchases.
The bank also said it would seek approval for various capital measures at this year's shareholder meeting.

Authorisation will be sought for a 200 million mark share issue, a 50 million mark share issue for employees, up to two billion marks in profit-sharing certificates and up to one billion marks for bonds with warrants and options.
All the authorisations will run until April 30, 2002.
A slight increase in Commerzbank's share capital to about two billion marks by the end of 1996 inflated the total dividend payout to 540 million marks.

The bank noted this was more than double the amount distributed four years ago and also said it planned to allocate 650 million marks of retained earnings to its revenue reserves, up from 400 million marks the previous year.

The rise in Commerzbank's operating earnings follows market leader Deutsche Bank AG's report of a 37 percent surge in operating profit to 5.8 billion marks. However, Deutsche managed only a 4.6 percent rise in net profit to 2.2 billion marks because of a surge in its tax charges.
Second-ranked Dresdner Bank AG is due to report its full 1996 results on Thursday.
